{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"A cool breeze stirred the grass, carrying the smell of rain and woodsmoke down into the valley. Mara pulled her coat tighter and glanced at the narrow path winding toward the village. She had meant to be home before dark, but the strange light on the ridge had stopped her.

It was there again: a small, steady glow between two boulders, too warm to be moonlight and too far away to belong to any cottage. Mara leaned forward, listening. From somewhere beyond the hills came three clear notes, like a bell struck underwater.

Her dog, Finn, gave a low whine.

“I hear it,” she whispered.

The glow vanished.

Mara stood still until the last strip of sunlight slipped from the sky. Then the bell sounded once more, closer now. Finn bolted toward the ridge, his lead slipping from her hand. She called after him, but the darkness swallowed the sound.

With a sigh, she followed.

The path climbed through thorn bushes and over loose stones. By the time she reached the boulders, the first stars had appeared. Finn waited beside a crack in the rock, tail stiff, eyes fixed on the ground. There, half buried in the moss, lay a brass key no longer than her thumb.

Its surface was warm.

Mara picked it up. A faint blue line ran along its shaft, brightening as she held it. Behind the boulders, something clicked.

The rock face shifted, opening a narrow seam of golden light.

From within came a voice she knew, though she had not heard it in years.

“Mara,” it said. “You’re late.”"}
